title: Distributed Key-Value Store (Dynamo)
summary: A highly available, partitioned KV store: consistent hashing with virtual nodes, N-way replication with tunable quorums, vector clocks or LWW for conflicts, hinted handoff, Merkle-tree anti-entropy and gossip membership.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: put(key, value), get(key); values up to ~1 MB
Always writable (AP): accept writes during partitions
Linear horizontal scale; no single point of failure

blocks.text: Ask for the read/write ratio and value size — they decide the storage engine and cache sizing.

items: Consistent hashing: hash(key) onto a ring; each physical node owns many **virtual nodes** so load and rebalancing spread evenly.
The key's **preference list** is the next N distinct physical nodes clockwise (spread across racks/AZs).
Adding a node moves only ~1/N of keys.

head: Setting
Meaning
Trade-off
rows: Reads see the latest acked write (absent sloppy quorum)

items: Conflicts from concurrent writes: **vector clocks** detect them and return siblings for the client to merge (Dynamo, Riak); or **last-write-wins** by timestamp (Cassandra) — simple but loses writes.
**Read repair:** on a read, replicas with stale versions are updated in the background.

items.title: Detect
items.text: Gossip: nodes exchange heartbeats/membership with random peers every second; phi-accrual detectors suspect failures.

items.title: Sloppy quorum
items.text: If a replica is down, write to the next healthy node with a hint.

items.title: Hinted handoff
items.text: When the owner recovers, the hint holder forwards the writes.

items.title: Anti-entropy
items.text: Replicas compare Merkle trees of key ranges and sync only differing subtrees.

items: Each node uses an LSM tree: writes go to a commit log + memtable, flush to immutable SSTables, compaction merges them.
Bloom filters per SSTable skip files that can't contain the key.
Deletes are tombstones that must outlive the longest replica outage (gc_grace) or deleted data resurrects.

cols.title: Leader-based (Raft per shard, e.g. TiKV)
cons: Unavailable for a shard during leader election / minority partition

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: I'd use consistent hashing with vnodes, N=3 with tunable R/W, sloppy quorum plus hinted handoff for availability, and Merkle trees to converge.

items.title: Scope
items.text: API, consistency needs (CP vs AP), value size.

items.q: Does W + R > N give linearizability?
items.a: No — with sloppy quorums, clock-based LWW or concurrent writes it doesn't; it gives overlap of acked sets in the happy path.

items.q: How do you add a node?
items.a: It takes vnodes from others; data streams over for those ranges; gossip spreads the new ring.

items.q: How do you handle a hot key?
items.a: Cache in front, replicate the key more widely, or split it into sub-keys at the application layer.

items: Ring + vnodes; preference list of N.
Gossip + sloppy quorum + hinted handoff + Merkle anti-entropy.
